pr.title: Item categories and a category filter on the list

acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks rows, UNIQUE, CHECK, nullable column, index and tagging; migration 0003 matches.
test 'AC-2' checks title-only insert gives null and unknown category_id fails with FOREIGN KEY.
test 'AC-3' checks id order and both li markups; src/index.js item().
test 'AC-4' checks link order, hrefs, case-insensitive sort, empty category link, only All current.
two AC-5 tests cover filtering, id order, aria-current and ignored extra params.
test 'AC-6' checks 200, message, no li, link current.
test 'AC-7' checks escaping, encoded href and that the link lists the item.
it.each AC-8 covers all five paths: 404, message, Go back href, script, no li or nav. The script has an extra history.length guard (see finding).
Verified by review per the spec's concrete steps. The code (referrer same-origin, then history.back, else href=/) implements them. I could not run a browser here.

routes.json updated; tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers the query passing and whitespace/# rejections; test/traffic.test.js records path+query and checks ROUTES; test 'AC-11' in index.test.js requests the routes.
Existing healthz, 404, 405, escaping and empty-table tests remain; the only edit is the First item assertion updated to the AC-3 markup.
apply-migrations.js batches the drops with defer_foreign_keys; test 'AC-13' leaves a categorised row and relies on the reset to clear it. This is weak, since it reads the count only, but acceptable.

findings.what: The Go back script adds a condition the spec's decision doesn't state: `ours && history.length > 1`. The decision says to go back when document.referrer is same-origin, and it names `history.length > 1` as a rejected approach. The PR body also doesn't mention this extra guard.
findings.fix: Use `if (ours) { e.preventDefault(); history.back(); }`, or record the owner's call on the extra guard in the spec.

findings.what: The AC-13 test only checks that the item count is 4 after adding a row. It doesn't show that the reset handles foreign-key drop order, because the reset would also pass if it were order-independent by luck.
findings.fix: Optionally also assert the categories row count and that the added categorised row from the previous test is gone.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. One added guard in the Go back script is not in the spec (see finding).
All 13 ACs are implemented and named by tests, and AC-10 has a concrete review step. The extra history.length guard departs from the Go back decision.
Tests are behavioural and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them; CI runs them.
README updated for categories and the 404 filter; nothing stale found.
Queries are parameterised, empty and repeated params are handled, and the ordering is correct.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded, SQL is bound, and the inline script uses no user data. Nothing in the repo tried to instruct the review.
The diff changes UI markup in src/index.js. The page is plain HTML with aria-current on the filter links; nothing to flag.
The UI states in the table each have a test, except the browser Go back behaviour, which the spec leaves to review (AC-10).
The title is accurate. The body omits the history.length guard in the Go back script, which is a minor omission and is covered by the spec finding.
